scoreRule: 1 point per correct MC item; 10 points maximum; local provisional grade only
description: Original film-review and environmental reading assessment, requiring independent linguistic and pedagogical validation

questions.q: What tension does the opening shot establish between the film's effects and its argument?
choices: A visual image can explain municipal waste contracts completely.
Feeling moved by an image is not the same as knowing how to act.
The choice of wrapper proves that the square is never cleaned.
The film's solemn style prevents viewers from noticing waste.
questions.explanation: The opening distinguishes the emotional reaction created by an image from practical knowledge.

questions.q: Why is the reviewer ambivalent about the beautiful images of night cleaners?
choices: The pictures exaggerate how dirty the public square was.
The shots hide that the workers separate recoverable waste.
The workers are shown only during daylight.
The workers gain admiration without much attention to their conditions.
questions.explanation: The beauty encourages respect for the workers but leaves their circumstances largely unexplained.

questions.q: What is achieved by the detailed recording of the cleaning sounds?
choices: It replaces the visual story with a council report.
It tells viewers exactly how to operate a recycling lorry.
It gives the night work a recognisable rhythm and presence.
It reveals that the cleaner's microphone was faulty.
questions.explanation: The precisely mixed sounds make the cleaners' usually unseen work more perceptible.

questions.q: Why does the cleaner's remark about five in the morning carry political force?
choices: It exposes the invisibility of work done for people who are absent.
It proves that the square should be cleaned only at night.
It shows that the workers prefer not to meet the public.
It indicates that recycling is less important than sweeping.
questions.explanation: The square is cleanest when no one sees the workers who made it clean.

questions.q: Which factor complicates the proposed cup-deposit system?
choices: The city has banned all reusable containers.
The film director will not interview the manager.
Stallholders require storage space and staff need training.
The scheme cannot operate without closing the square.
questions.explanation: The manager explains the need for space, training and equipment, not merely enthusiasm.

questions.q: What is lost when the narrative returns to the teenager dropping a bottle?
choices: Attention shifts from the design of infrastructure to guilt about an individual.
The film no longer contains any images of rubbish.
The director abandons visual storytelling in favour of statistics.
The cleaner becomes the main character of the documentary.
questions.explanation: The repeated slow-motion image moves the question away from systems towards moral blame.

questions.q: What is the significance of the different ways people appear in the film?
choices: All characters are presented as equally authoritative.
Names and opportunities to explain are distributed unevenly.
The manager and cleaners are filmed in identical ways.
The teenager is the only person permitted to speak.
questions.explanation: The reviewer contrasts anonymous workers and a nameless teenager with a manager allowed to explain.

questions.q: What does the volunteer's admission about extra washing trips show?
choices: Reusable containers have been disproved as an environmental approach.
The film should focus more strongly on beautiful scenery.
Environmental projects are credible only if nothing goes wrong.
Acknowledging an unexpected cost can make a proposal more credible.
questions.explanation: The volunteer's uncertainty invites revision rather than either celebration or dismissal.

questions.q: What more would the reviewer have wanted the film to reveal?
choices: A final numerical ranking of all the cleaners.
A detailed account of every concert that took place.
The systems and practical decisions surrounding a visible piece of litter.
An explanation of the director's personal motivation for filming.
questions.explanation: The conclusion wishes the system around the wrapper had been made as visible as the wrapper.

questions.q: What does the reviewer imply about film-making and public argument?
choices: Choices about representation carry an argument even without explicit commentary.
A documentary should show spreadsheets after every emotional scene.
The visual form of a film is unrelated to what it communicates.
All political documentaries must avoid music and visual surprise.
questions.explanation: The reviewer notes that decisions about who is named and seen are themselves arguments.
